key_idea: Any dissection of a rectangle into at most four rectangles is guillotine (a non-guillotine pinwheel needs five), so recursively split the piece set in two with a straight vertical or horizontal cut.
sketch: The total area must be a perfect square S^2. tile(set, W, H): a single piece must equal WxH up to rotation; otherwise for every proper non-empty subset, if its area is divisible by H try a vertical cut at area/H and recurse on both sides, and likewise horizontally with W. With 4 pieces this is a handful of states. Pitfalls: rotations are handled only at the leaves, sub-rectangle dimensions must be positive integers, and all layouts (2x2 grid, strips, 1+3, T-shapes) are covered by the recursion rather than by hand-enumerated cases.
